title: Igor Girkin
description: Russian intelligence officer and militant leader (born 1970)
wiki_lead:
Igor Vsevolodovich Girkin (Russian: Игорь Всеволодович Гиркин, IPA: [ˈiɡərʲ ˈfsʲevələdəvʲɪdʑ ˈɡʲirkʲɪn]; born 17 December 1970), also known by the alias Igor Ivanovich Strelkov (Russian: Игорь Иванович Стрелков, IPA: [ˈiɡərʲ ɪˈvanəvʲɪtɕ strʲɪlˈkof]), is a Russian army veteran and former Federal Security Service (FSB) officer who played a key role in the Russian annexation of Crimea, and then in the Donbas War as an organizer of militant groups in the Donetsk People's Republic (DPR). In 2024 he was convicted on charges of inciting extremism. Earlier he received a life sentence in absentia in the Netherlands for his role in downing the Malaysia Airlines Flight 17.
Girkin admitted responsibility for sparking the Donbas War in eastern Ukraine when, in April 2014, he led a group of armed Russian militants who seized Sloviansk. His role in the siege gained him influence and attention, and he was appointed to the position of Minister of Defense in the Donetsk People's Republic, a puppet state of Russia. Girkin was charged with terrorism by Ukrainian authorities. He has also been sanctioned by the European Union, United States, United Kingdom, Australia, Japan, Canada and Switzerland for his leading role in the war in eastern Ukraine.
Girkin was dismissed from his position in August 2014, after 298 civilians were killed when Malaysia Airlines Flight 17 was shot down by Russian-backed militants. Dutch prosecutors charged Girkin and three others with mass murder, and issued an international arrest warrant against him.  Girkin admitted "moral responsibility" but denied pushing the button. On 17 November 2022, Girkin was found guilty for the murder of 298 people, convicted of all charges in absentia, and issued a life sentence.
Girkin is a self-described Russian nationalist. After his service in the war, he returned to Russia in 2014 as a political activist, reportedly calling for the liberal part of the Russian elite to be destroyed, which would shift the power balance in favor of militarists and securocrats.
During the Russian invasion of Ukraine, Girkin regained attention as a milblogger, taking a strong pro-war stance but criticizing the Russian military for what he saw as incompetence and "insufficiency". In October 2022, Girkin briefly joined a volunteer unit fighting against Ukrainian forces. In April 2023, Girkin, alongside some fellow Russian nationalists joined the Club of Angry Patriots, a hardline pro-war group. He began criticizing Vladimir Putin for incompetence and on 21 July 2023 was arrested by Russian authorities on charges of extremism. Girkin was convicted in January 2024 of inciting extremism and sentenced to four years' imprisonment.

grok_lead: Igor Vsevolodovich Girkin (born 17 December 1970), known by the nom de guerre Igor Strelkov, is a former officer of Russia's Federal Security Service (FSB) and a veteran of multiple post-Soviet armed conflicts, most notably as the field commander who initiated the separatist insurgency in Ukraine's Donetsk Oblast in April 2014 by leading the seizure of Sloviansk. Born in Moscow to a military family with a background in historical reenactments and studies at the Moscow State Institute of History and Archives, Girkin served in Russia's Air Defense Forces from 1993 to 1994 before joining the FSB in 1996, where he rose to the rank of colonel by his retirement in 2013, participating in operations in Chechnya from 1999 to 2005. Earlier, as a young volunteer, he fought with pro-Russian forces in Transnistria in 1992 and Serb militias in Bosnia from 1992 to 1993. In the 2014 Donbass conflict, Girkin commanded the pro-Russian separatist forces that captured government buildings in Sloviansk, an action he later described as the spark that ignited the war, and briefly held the position of defense minister in the self-proclaimed Donetsk People's Republic before his unit's retreat from the city in July. His role extended to overseeing the deployment of a Buk missile system implicated in the July 2014 downing of Malaysia Airlines Flight 17, for which a Dutch court convicted him in absentia of murder in 2022, sentencing him to life imprisonment. After returning to Russia, Girkin transitioned into a public commentator and ultranationalist blogger, frequently criticizing President Vladimir Putin's strategic decisions and the perceived incompetence in conducting military operations against Ukraine. Girkin's outspoken advocacy for a more aggressive approach in the conflict led to his arrest by Russian authorities in July 2023 on charges of inciting extremism, stemming from public statements accusing Putin of weakness; he was convicted and sentenced to four years in prison in January 2024, with his appeal denied later that year. Despite his imprisonment, Girkin remains a polarizing figure among Russian nationalists, admired by some for his combat experience and forthrightness but viewed warily by the Kremlin for his intransigence.
